text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's Committee for environmental protection has halted operations at 58 businesses which seriously violated environment regulations.

-- The main cause of strikes in Vietnam relate to unfair salaries, working hours and annual leave for employees and most of the labour conflicts occur at small-scale foreign-invested enteprises, particularly those involving Korean, Singaporean and Taiwanese capital, research by the Labour Ministry revealed.
-- The trade ministers of Vietnam and Cambodia are expected to review preparations for a trade agreement during a working visit to Vietnam by a Cambodian trade mission July 7-11.

-- Vietnam is expected to attract around $5.5 billion of foreign direct investment (FDI) in such key areas as industry, agriculture and infrastructure in 1998. Next year 20 major FDI projects now under negotiation are likely to be licensed.

-- Vietnam is considered by the Australian government as an important partner with which Australia is committed to developing a long-standing cooperation relationship, Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Wednesday in talks with Vietnam's Foreign Minister, Nguyen Manh Cam.
-- The Politburo of the Communist Party has ordered celebrations of the 20th anniversary of the signing of the Vietnam-Laos Agreement on friendship and cooperation on July 18.
-- The Government Pricing Committee's target for the second half of 1997 will be to avoid declining market prices which could affect the speed of growth, exports and harm production.

-- Burkina Faso Foreign Minister Ablasse Ouedraogo is due to arrive in Hanoi on Thursday to bolster relations between the two countries and discuss measures to implement an agreement signed last November on economic, trade, cultural and other cooperation.
-- Vietnam Airlines recently bought two Airbus A320 and ATR72 cabins from France at a cost of $2 million for training its air hostess staff.
